label: prf:feynman-categorical-trace
title: Proof of Feynman transition amplitude as categorical trace
html:
Proof. The argument proceeds in three steps. By (eigenbasis decomposition), the algebraic state space V_{\mathrm{phys}} = \varinjlim V^{\otimes n} decomposes into the finite eigenbasis \bigoplus_\lambda V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda on which the braid \beta \in B_n acts. By (trace collapse), the Feynman path integral on this eigenbasis collapses to a finite weighted sum over the irreducible summands, with no regularisation needed. By (Markov identification), this Markov-weighted sum equals the Jones--Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr) in H_n(R, q), and the Markov weights are w_\lambda = \dim_q(V_\lambda) \cdot \dim(S_\lambda) / \dim_q(V^{\otimes n}).

By the categorical mass as Markov trace (categorical mass as Markov trace), the absolute value of this expression is the categorical mass at a single brane level: \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)|_{\text{single level}} = |\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))|. \square
